title: Triage clustering splits identical findings into separate tickets
body:
Observed live while triaging the shared corpus at /tmp/af-corpus with two sessions (claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-fable-5, both family 'claude', tier 'volume').

Two tickets were written for what is plainly ONE finding:

  qa/tickets/S3-bug-32518b294a7c96af.json
    'wolf_winter quest opening room steading_yard, blocked exit north'
  qa/tickets/S3-bug-974802c3fd041c01.json
    'quest wolf_winter, room steading_yard, blocked exit north'

Same quest, same room, same blocked exit, same severity S3 — reported independently by two different models, which is exactly the corroboration signal triage exists to detect. They did not merge into one cluster.

Across the run the split is total, not occasional: session 1 produced 12 issues -> 12 clusters; adding session 2 produced 23 issues -> 23 clusters. Not a single issue merged across the two sessions.

Promotion impact here is nil — both models are family 'claude', so a merged cluster would still have families.length === 1 and still sit at 'accumulating' per derivePromotion. But once a second vendor family is in the corpus, this failure to merge is the difference between 'corroborated' (actionable) and two 'accumulating' tickets nobody picks up. It silently defeats the corroboration rung.

Also worth a look while in there: ticket 'title' has a stemmed token bag prepended before an '@' separator, e.g. 'action albany approach block both cannot @ wolf_winter quest opening room steading_yard...'. That cluster signature leaking into the human-facing title is what makes near-duplicates hard to eyeball in qa:bucket output.
